title: Network pharmacology and molecular docking-based strategy to determine the potential mechanism for escitalopram-mediated long QT syndrome.
authors: Zhuo, Chuanjun; Zhang, Ying; Li, Chao; Yang, Lei; Zhang, Qiuyu; Li, Ranli; Tian, Hongjun; Mao, Fuqiang
one_liner_zh: 该文用网络药理学和分子对接研究艾司西酞普兰致长QT综合征的机制，虽含分子对接但对象为药物-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: The objective of this study was to identify the potential molecular mechanisms for escitalopram-mediated development of long QT syndrome (LQTS) using network pharmacology and molecular docking. METHOD: Targets related to LQTS were obtained from the GeneCards, DisGeNET, and OMIM databases, while targets related to escitalopram were retrieved from the PharmMapper, SwissTargetPrediction, SuperPred, GeneCards, DrugBank, and SEA databases. A Venn diagram containing drug-disease intersection targets was generated using the Bioinformatics online tool. A protein-protein interaction network was developed using the STRING database. Core targets were screened using Cytoscape, and Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses of escitalopram-LQTS intersection targets were performed using DAVID. A drug-disease-target pathway network was developed with Cytoscape. AutoDock Vina and PyMOL software were used for molecular docking analyses. RESULTS: Six potential targets of escitalopram-mediated LQTS, including TNF, IL-1beta, INS, SRC, STAT3, and GSK-3beta, were shown to bind well to escitalopram in molecular docking analyses. The KEGG enrichment analysis suggested that escitalopram caused adverse LQTS reactions by modulating prolactin and lipid levels, atherosclerosis, and the calcium signaling pathway. LIMITATIONS: Further in vitro or molecular biology experiments are needed to validate the mechanism identified in this study by which escitalopram induced LQTS. CONCLUSIONS: Based on bioinformatic analysis, escitalopram may affect the electrolyte balance, atherosclerosis, and ion channels implicated in LQTS, providing theoretical clues for follow-up studies.
abstract_zh: 背景：本研究旨在利用网络药理学和分子对接技术，探讨艾司西酞普兰介导的长QT综合征（LQTS）的潜在分子机制。方法：从GeneCards、DisGeNET和OMIM数据库获取与LQTS相关的靶点，同时从PharmMapper、SwissTargetPrediction、SuperPred、GeneCards、DrugBank和SEA数据库检索与艾司西酞普兰相关的靶点。使用Bioinformatics在线工具生成包含药物-疾病交集靶点的维恩图。利用STRING数据库构建蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络。使用Cytoscape筛选核心靶点，并通过DAVID对艾司西酞普兰-LQTS交集靶点进行基因本体论（GO）和京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）富集分析。使用Cytoscape构建药物-疾病-靶点通路网络。分子对接分析采用AutoDock Vina和PyMOL软件。结果：分子对接分析显示，艾司西酞普兰介导LQTS的六个潜在靶点，包括TNF、IL-1beta、INS、SRC、STAT3和GSK-3beta，均与艾司西酞普兰结合良好。KEGG富集分析提示，艾司西酞普兰通过调节催乳素和脂质水平、动脉粥样硬化及钙信号通路，引起不良LQTS反应。局限性：需要进一步的体外或分子生物学实验来验证本研究中确定的艾司西酞普兰诱导LQTS的机制。结论：基于生物信息学分析，艾司西酞普兰可能影响与LQTS相关的电解质平衡、动脉粥样硬化和离子通道，为后续研究提供理论线索。
